rationale: The Latin anchor *caro* consistently refers to the physical flesh/soft tissue of the body (as in "spiritus promptus est, caro autem infirma" and "caro enim mea vere est cibus"), contrasting spirit with bodily flesh and referencing it as food/drink, which aligns directly with flesh.n.01 (soft tissue of the body). The attestations from biblical passages (Mt., Mk., Jn., Gen.) confirm the literal, physical sense of flesh as bodily tissue rather than the whole human body (human_body.n.01) or fruit pulp (pulp.n.02).
